unit.why: A short narrative: R. Zvi sees R. Menachem Mendel of Rymanów bend his thumb under his four fingers and wishes to attain it before his death; on his death day his brother sees him do so and weeps, knowing he will die.

stories.start_quote: פ"א ראה רבינו צבי איך הרה״ק
stories.summary_en: R. Zvi saw R. Menachem Mendel of Rymanów fold his thumb under his four fingers, bowing all his limbs to God, and wished to attain this before his death; on the day he died his brother R. Moshe saw him make the same gesture and wept, knowing he was about to pass away.

tags.why: The narrative culminates in R. Zvi's deathbed sign.

quotes: והנה ביום פטירתו של רבינו צבי
tags.why: The day of the tsaddik's death is depicted.

quotes: ראה אותו אחיו הרה״ק רבי ר' משה
tags.why: His brother R. Moshe is a character.

quotes: ראה רבינו צבי איך הרה״ק רבינו מנחם מענדל מרימונאב
tags.why: R. Zvi observes and emulates his master of Rymanów.
A bodily gesture of total submission and cleaving to God.
The brother cries out and weeps.
The gesture is read as a sign of imminent death, fulfilling R. Zvi's wish.
The brother recognises the meaning of the gesture.
